title: Fine-tuning versus giving information in a request

sections.skill: Tell fine-tuning from supplying information in a request

questions.prompt: A company trains an existing model further on 20,000 of its own support chats. What is this?

choices.text: Deleting the model's parameters
Inference on 20,000 new questions
Fine-tuning, which changes the model
Supplying information in a request

questions.correct_answer: Fine-tuning, which changes the model
questions.intro: There are two very different ways to make a model handle your needs. FINE-TUNING is more training: a model that already exists is trained further on new examples, which changes its parameters. It takes data, time and skill, and the change lasts for every later use of that tuned version. SUPPLYING INFORMATION IN THE REQUEST means putting what the model needs, such as a policy document, a list of rules or a few examples, into your message or an attached file. That does not change the model; it only affects that request (and that conversation, while the text stays in context).
questions.feedback: Training further on new examples is fine-tuning.

It is fine-tuned on the school rules forever

sections.skill: Compare a training course with a note on the desk

questions.prompt: Fine-tuning is like which option?

choices.text: Both options
The note left on the desk
The weeks-long training course
Neither option

questions.correct_answer: The weeks-long training course
questions.intro: A new employee can learn about a company in two ways. She can attend a TRAINING COURSE for weeks, and what she learns stays with her afterward. Or her manager can leave a NOTE on her desk: "Today the store closes at 6." The note helps today, but it does not change her training, and tomorrow there may be a different note. Fine-tuning is like the training course: it changes the model. Putting information in a request is like the note: it helps with that task and changes nothing permanent.
questions.feedback: Further training changes the learner.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Decide when fine-tuning is the wrong tool

questions.prompt: A store wants a model to know its 2,000 prices, which change weekly. Why is fine-tuning a poor fit?

choices.text: Prices are illegal to share with any AI model
Prices change weekly; fine-tuning suits that poorly
Fine-tuning works only for images
Fine-tuning cannot use numbers at all

questions.correct_answer: Prices change weekly; fine-tuning suits that poorly
questions.intro: Choosing between the two depends on the job. For facts that change often, like this week's prices or a policy updated monthly, supplying current information in the request is usually easier to keep up to date. Fine-tuning suits teaching a lasting style or format across many uses, or a specialized task with lots of examples. Fine-tuning is NOT a reliable way to make a model "know" a long list of changing facts, and it can introduce new mistakes. Either way, results need testing, and private data used for fine-tuning needs the same care as any other data sharing.
questions.feedback: Changing facts are better supplied from a current source.
